description:
The reconciler is **not** a GenServer. It is a pure functional
module over an immutable `%UI.State{}` value:

  * `UI.State.new(root_component, props)` — initial state.
  * `UI.State.handle_key(state, %Key{}) :: state` — fold a key event
    through hook subscriptions, return updated state.
  * `UI.State.handle_event(state, term) :: state` — same for
    arbitrary messages routed to a hole (streaming snapshots,
    timer wakeups, etc.).
  * `UI.State.tick(state, now_ms) :: state` — advance frame clock;
    invalidates any holes whose `use_frame` deadline has passed.
  * `UI.State.paint(state, %RenderContext{}) :: {state, iodata, cursor_or_nil}`
    — single-pass paint; returns updated state (memo cache,
    visited-cell GC) plus the bytes the renderer will diff.
  * `UI.State.dirty?(state) :: boolean` — has any cell been
    invalidated since the last paint? Drives the
    paint-or-skip decision in Interactive's :timeout handler.
  * `UI.State.next_wait_ms(state) :: non_neg_integer() | :infinity`
    — earliest pending deadline. Combines (a) animation deadlines
    from active `use_frame` cells, (b) the max-staleness cap
    (`dirty_since_ms + max_staleness_ms`, default ~16ms) that
    prevents paint starvation under continuous event pressure.

Hook handle `h` carries a reference to the hole's cell within the
state value. Hook-cell values are stored by identity, never
deep-compared — components hold large structs (e.g. %MdRender{})
in cells and the only "changed" signal is an explicit setter call.

Setters returned from hooks call back into UI.State to produce a
new state value (no message sends). Setters called *during render*
fold into the same paint pass — React's "derived state from props"
pattern. Documented and tested explicitly.

Hooks delivered: `use_state`, `use_memo`, `use_frame`, `use_key`,
`use_effect`. Hook-cell GC: cells not visited during a paint are
retained one frame, then dropped — implemented as a generation
counter on the state value, no GenServer timers.

**Interactive integration (the mailbox-drain + debounce model):**

State-mutating handlers in Interactive (`:hid`, `:stream_delta`,
`:bash_done`, etc.) fold the event into UI.State and return
`{:noreply, state, min(debounce_ms, UI.State.next_wait_ms(ui))}`
— they do **not** paint inline. The `:timeout` handler is the only
place that paints, and only when `UI.State.dirty?/1` returns true.

The GenServer's "timeout fires only when the mailbox is empty"
semantics give us free burst coalescing: 12 streaming deltas
arriving back-to-back become 1 paint. The max-staleness cap inside
`next_wait_ms/1` prevents starvation under continuous event
pressure.

Tests: pure-function tests over `UI.State` — feed a key sequence,
assert the resulting state's painted bytes; assert `next_wait_ms`
coalesces correctly across multiple animated holes; assert memo
invalidation triggers repaint of just the affected subtree; assert
`dirty?/1` flips correctly across paint cycles; assert max-staleness
bound under simulated event pressure.
title: Reconciler state + hooks (pure functions; Interactive drives the loop)
